name: West Virginia
summary: Statutes: code.wvlegislature.gov serves one page per section at a URL built from the citation (/55-7-8a/), readable by WebFetch and the script, plus whole-chapter PDFs (/pdf/55/); the old www.wvlegislature.gov/WVCODE/ viewer is robots-blocked; Justia 2025 is the tier-2 fallback. The constitution is one long page on code.wvlegislature.gov (WebFetch stops in Art. VII) with a second Legislature copy and Justia. Court rules are single long HTML pages on courtswv.gov (all beyond the WebFetch window: corpus candidates). Code of State Rules: Secretary of State final-file PDFs via id hops (old rules are image scans); Cornell LII mirrors it but can be decades stale; the State Register PDFs are image-only. Case law: courtswv.gov archives (Supreme Court 1991-, ICA 2022-) are searchable by plain GET; slip pagination only; subsequent history by party name.

citation_map.notes: West Virginia Code sections are always chapter-article-section (55-7-8a); the URL is https://code.wvlegislature.gov/{chapter}-{article}-{section}/ with letters in either case (site links use upper case: 55-7-8A). Older state and court style writes '§55-7-8a' with no 'W. Va. Code' prefix and the prose form 'section 8a, article 7, chapter 55 of the Code of West Virginia'; the bare § form is context_required because Kentucky-, Tennessee- and Arkansas-style three-part numbers look the same. A '§§ 55-7-13a to -13d' range is a span: the regex takes only the first section (the (?![\w-]) guard keeps '13a' from swallowing the range). Code of State Rules: Bluebook 'W. Va. Code R. § 110-1H-1' = title 110, series 1H, section 1; the SOS lookup key pads the series to two digits (110-01H) while Cornell LII uses the unpadded form (110-1H-1). Case law: the official reporter is West Virginia Reports (W. Va.), printed by West with S.E./S.E.2d parallels; neither is free online, so free texts carry slip pagination only. West Virginia opinions put holdings in numbered syllabus points ('Syl. Pt. 3'), which are cited as pinpoints. Memorandum decisions are citable under R. App. P. 21(e) if labelled '(memorandum decision)'. The Intermediate Court of Appeals (W. Va. Ct. App.) has decided cases since July 2022 with dockets 'YY-ICA-N'. No public-domain citation format exists. Bare 'Rule N of the Rules of Civil Procedure', bare dockets and syllabus points are generic and route only with West Virginia context. CourtListener ids 'wva' and 'wvactapp' are from memory and unverified. Westlaw cites ('2023 WL …') cannot be resolved to a free URL: search by party name instead.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Legislature
sources.official_status_evidence: Footer says only 'These West Virginia Code sections are updated regularly as new legislation takes effect' and refers to the Bill Status database for effective dates; no official-version or UELMA authentication statement found (https://code.wvlegislature.gov/55-7-8a/). The annotated Michie's West Virginia Code (LexisNexis) is the printed edition.
sources.coverage: All chapters 1-64 of the West Virginia Code; one HTML page per section, with bill history ('Bill History For §55-7-8a') and links to enrolled bills.

access.pattern_rules: chapter, article and section exactly as cited, joined by hyphens, letters kept (55-7-8a, 61-2-1, 29A-5-4); letter case does not matter (site links use 55-7-8A, lower-case 55-7-8a also serves the section). Article TOC: https://code.wvlegislature.gov/{chapter}-{article}/ (lists every section with its heading, no text); chapter TOC: https://code.wvlegislature.gov/{chapter}/ (lists articles). A complete section index (every section link on one page) is https://www.wvlegislature.gov/wvcodeentire.htm.
